title: Take the temporary prop out from under a repaired shelf without dragging the shelf off its brackets
keywords: hold while the other arm works
instruction: The shelf's right-hand bracket has been replaced, but the red prop that held the shelf up is still under it. Take the prop out and put it on the blue mat, leaving the shelf on both brackets with the tin of soup still standing on it.
context: Props, jack stands and clamps that carry a load during a repair are often left in afterwards, where they block the space they stand in and hide whether the permanent support really carries the load. Here the shelf still rests on the prop, 8 mm clear of the new bracket, so pulling the prop straight out drags the shelf's free end with it and drops it, and knocking the prop over drops the load onto a bracket nobody has checked; the load has to be taken off the prop first and then set down on the bracket.
setup: On the table, all positions as x (cm forward of the line joining the two arm bases) and y (cm left of the midline between the arms). Two grey steel brackets, each a block 6 cm front to back, 4 cm wide and 8 cm high, fixed to the table with centres at (30, +18) and (30, -18). A pine shelf board, 40 cm long, 6 cm wide, 1.8 cm thick, 0.22 kg, loose, lying across them along y with its centre at (30, 0); its ends are flush with the brackets' outer faces. A red-painted timber prop, 12 cm long, 4 cm wide, 8.8 cm high, 0.15 kg, loose, standing on the table under the shelf with its long side pointing at the arms and its centre at (27, -10), so its front 6 cm sticks out in front of the shelf. Because the prop is 8 mm taller than the brackets, the shelf rests on the prop and on the left bracket, sloping 1.6 degrees, with an 8 mm gap over the right bracket. A full tin of soup (steel can with a paper label, 6.7 cm diameter, 10.2 cm tall, 0.35 kg, loose) standing on the shelf with its centre at (30, +15); it is 7 mm wider than the shelf and overhangs the front and back edges equally. A blue rubber mat, 16 cm front to back, 8 cm wide, 0.4 cm thick, fixed to the table with its centre at (18, -24). Three distractors stand loose on the table behind the shelf and play no part in scoring: a red ceramic mug (9 cm diameter, 8 cm tall, 11.4 cm across with its handle, 0.30 kg) with its body centred at (48, +24) and its handle pointing at the arms; a roll of clear packing tape (10 cm diameter, 5 cm wide, 0.06 kg) lying flat with its centre at (49, -22); and a Phillips screwdriver (18.8 cm long, 3.4 cm across the handle, 0.10 kg) lying parallel to the shelf at x = 47, reaching from y = -5 to y = +14. Two arms with parallel grippers, bases at (0, +30.5) and (0, -30.5).
scoring: Scored on the final state, once everything is at rest, except that three events count whenever they happen. 0 if at any time the tin tips more than 30 degrees or comes off the shelf (its centre lower than the brackets' tops), any part of the shelf drops more than 3 cm below the brackets' tops, or the prop tips more than 30 degrees while any part of it is under the shelf seen from above (knocking the prop over instead of taking the load off it). Otherwise 1.0 if all of these hold: the shelf lies on both brackets (each end at least 1 cm onto its bracket and within 3 cm of the bracket's centre line front to back, its underside within 4 mm of the brackets' tops, one end no more than 4 mm higher than the other); the tin stands on the shelf within 10 degrees of upright; seen from above, no part of the prop overlaps the shelf; the prop rests on the blue mat with its centre over the mat; and neither end of the shelf is more than 2 cm from where it started. 0.5 if the shelf lies on both brackets, the tin stands on it and no part of the prop overlaps the shelf seen from above, but the prop is not on the mat or an end of the shelf has moved more than 2 cm. 0 in every other case, including doing nothing, the prop still under the shelf (standing or lying), and the shelf, tin or prop still moving or held off its resting place at the end. The distractors are not scored.
reset_notes: Nothing is consumed. To reset, stand the prop at (27, -10), lay the shelf on the prop and the left bracket with its ends at y = +20 and -20, and stand the tin at (30, +15). Put back any distractor that was moved.
fidelity: The brackets, shelf, prop and mat are rigid boxes; the tin of soup and the three distractors are NVIDIA SimReady props with their masses set by hand (the tin and the screwdriver collide as convex hulls). Everything moves under gravity and friction only; nothing is jointed, glued or screwed. The brackets are plain fixed blocks standing on the table rather than wall-mounted angle brackets, and there is no wall behind the shelf. Every surface has the same high friction (1.2 static, 1.0 dynamic, rubber-like), which is higher than wood on steel and makes the shelf follow a dragged prop more readily than a real one would. The tin is one rigid body with no liquid moving inside. The scorer reads object poses only: there is no force sensing, it cannot tell whether a gripper is still touching an object beyond requiring the shelf, tin and prop to be at rest, and it judges that the new bracket carries the shelf only from the shelf's final position, not from any checking action. The task is at table scale (a 40 cm shelf and a 9 cm prop), smaller than a typical shelf repair, and the 8 mm gap over the new bracket is hard to see from the top camera; the prop sticking out in front of the shelf is the visible sign.
